# Part 1: Environment isolation
This activity highlights important differences in how `venv` and `conda` create “isolated” environments.

:::{.card .border-primary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Getting Started
:::

:::{.card-body}
#### 1. Record the path to your base `python3` executable
- Use `command` and `realpath` to expose the source of your `python3` executable.
  Record this path in the box below for future reference.

```bash
realpath $(command -v python3)
```

<span class="text-primary">Record path below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

:::
:::


:::{.card .border-primary .mb-3}
:::{.card-header}
## Venv
:::

:::{.card-body}
#### 2. Create and activate a new `venv` environment
- Create a new `venv` environment called `test_env_1`
  ```bash
  python3 -m venv test_env_1
  ```

- Activate your new environment
  ```bash
  source test_env_1/bin/activate
  ```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
You can revert to a clean state at any time with:  
`deactivate; rm -r test_env_1/`
:::

#### 3. Determine the location of your Python executable in the `test_env_1` environment
- Expose the executable path using `command` and `realpath`.

```bash
realpath $(command -v python3)
```

<span class="text-primary">Record path below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

:::{.card .border-primary .mb-4}
:::{.card-header}
## Conda / Mamba
:::

:::{.card-body}
#### 4. Create and activate a new conda environment
- Create a new `conda` environment called `test_env_1`
  ```bash
  conda create -n test_env_1 python
  ```

- Activate your new environment
  ```bash
  conda activate test_env_1
  ```

#### 5. Determine the location of your Python executable again
- Use `command` and `realpath` to determine if the Python executable path changed.

```bash
realpath $(command -v python3)
```

<span class="text-primary">Record path below:</span>
<div class="textbox textbox-editable" contenteditable="true"></div>

**5.1 Is this the same as your base `python3` path?**

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio" id="conda-yes" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda-yes">Yes</label>

  <input type="radio" class="btn-check" name="conda-radio" id="conda-no" autocomplete="off">
  <label class="btn btn-outline-primary" for="conda-no">No</label>
</div>

#### 6. Deactivate the conda environment
- Return to your base environment:
  ```bash
  conda deactivate
  ```

- Confirm you are no longer in `test_env_1`:
  ```bash
  conda info --envs
  ```

#### 7. (Optional) Remove the conda environment entirely
- Permanently delete the `test_env_1` environment:
  ```bash
  conda env remove -n test_env_1
  ```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Unlike `venv`, conda environments live outside your project directory.  
Removing them requires an explicit `conda env remove`.
:::

:::
:::
